design_detail: Repeat PET of striatal DAT availability in a small subset of methamphetamine users after protracted abstinence (about 12–17 months), compared with their earlier scans.
can_establish: That DAT availability can increase substantially with abstinence in individual users.
cannot_establish: Generalizable magnitude (n = 5); whether function recovers in step with the marker.

sample.recruitment: Subset of the earlier PET cohort who remained abstinent.
sample.selection_effects: Those who stayed abstinent and returned; likely the least severe cases.

exposure.measurement: As in the original cohort; abstinence verified [to be extracted from PDF]
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: 12–17 months ([to be extracted from PDF] exact)

comparison.controls: Within-person (baseline scan) and the original control group.

outcomes.instruments: PET DAT; motor and memory tasks.
outcomes.operationalization: Change in binding and in task scores.

analysis.effect_sizes: DAT increased substantially ([to be extracted from PDF] %); task performance improved less ([to be extracted from PDF]).

interpretation_gap.results_show: Recovery of the biomarker with abstinence in a tiny sample.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Often omitted from accounts that cite the 2001 association paper as showing permanent damage.

timeline.event: Partial recovery of regional brain glucose metabolism after protracted abstinence

replication.where_it_stands: Reversibility of some markers is supported; extent and functional correlates remain uncertain.

what_would_settle_it: Larger longitudinal imaging cohorts with verified abstinence and functional outcomes.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Tiny, selected follow-up sample; valuable mainly as proof that the marker is not fixed.
